The Gap Between Expectations and Reality

Speaking on behalf of Architecht at the Webrazzi Fintech 2025 event, Zeynep Erdoğan analyzed the root causes of the disappointments organizations have experienced with their AI projects. The presentation, which cited Gartner data, highlighted the adoption timelines of these technologies. The fact that ChatGPT reached the same audience that the automobile took 33 years and the telephone took 15 years to reach in just two months has created a level of expectation that is difficult to manage on the corporate side.

In the fintech sector in particular, the inability to use public cloud solutions due to regulations is pushing organizations to build their own internal GPT infrastructures. However, the tendency of technical teams to adopt technologies such as blockchain or artificial intelligence simply because they are popular negatively impacts the sustainability of projects and their ability to generate value.

A Three-Tiered Strategy: Need, Impact, and Technology

For AI investments to succeed, value must be prioritized over technology. Erdoğan addresses this process through three fundamental layers:

  • Business Need: First, the targeted business and the problem must be clearly defined.
  • Impact Analysis: Discussing the added value the defined business will create and its effects on the process.
  • Technology Selection: In the final stage, identifying the most suitable technology to meet the defined need.

Pilot and Scaling Processes

It is noted that massive AI models are not required to solve every problem; sometimes, a simple Robotic Process Automation (RPA) solution can produce more efficient results. When designing solutions, gathering feedback from end users and establishing measurable metrics are of critical importance. Scaling pilot projects based on feasibility reports emerges as a key factor in preventing resource waste and ensuring the project’s success.
